newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Argentina sees jobless down to 5-6 pct in 4 years.
newsitem.headline: Argentina sees jobless down to 5-6 pct in 4 years.

text.p: Argentina's unemployment rate would fall to a natural rate of about five or six percent over the next four years if reforms to labour laws were sucessfully implemented, Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said on Tuesday.
Argentina's unemployment rate stood at 17.1 percent in the most recent official survey taken in May.
"The new legislation in terms of labour contracts will help to reduce unemployment," Fernandez told a media briefing in Melbourne.
Fernandez is in Melbourne's for Australia's National Trade and Investment Conference.

He said the government hoped the new laws, which modify the collective bargaining process and replace severance payments with unemployment insurance, would be passed this year, possibly within the next two weeks.

"If we enact the new labour legislation, I think our natural rate of unemployment -- that will imply just transitory unemployed searching for a better job -- that could be around five percent, six percent," he said.
Fernandez repeated that he did not expect survey results for October to be released later this month to show any fall in the 17.1 percent unemployment rate measured in May.
He said the lagging effect on unemployment of the pick-up this year in economic activity meant the rate would not start to fall until 1997.
He said he expected the rate to fall by at least two percentage points in 1997, but that some analysts had forecast a five point fall if the reforms were sucessful.

"If it is true that we can jam the five points in one year as a concequence of this modification, then I think easy we can reduce the unemployment rate by two additional points per year (in each following year)," he said.
"That would imply that in about four years we will be in the order of five or six percent," he said.

The labour reforms include the ending of all current labour contracts so that they are renegotiated at the level of the firm rather than at industry level and the removal of the current severance payment system with an unemployment insurance system where the employer pays four percent of a workers wages into individual unemployment insurance accounts.

Fernandez said the economy was now recovering from the 1995 recession bought on by the Mexican peso devaluation of late 1994 and that he now saw economic growth for the full 1996 year of about three percent.
He also said the government saw growth rising to five percent in 1997. The government's budget approved late last month forecast five percent GDP growth in 1997.
